look_here_first: Find a tall riparian cottonwood with alternate, broadly ovate to heart-shaped finely serrated leaves (spring leaves may look narrower), sticky reddish-brown aromatic winter buds, and pale whitish leaf undersides. Confirm long hanging catkins, cottony seed capsules and twig/bud characters; separate from local Populus deltoides using blade shape, undersides, petiole and fine margin teeth.

taxonomic_note: POWO/WCVP accepts Populus tristis Fisch. and treats Populus trichocarpa Torr. & A.Gray ex Hook. as a synonym; Flora of North America and USDA use Populus trichocarpa as the working accepted name. These refer to the same Western North American black cottonwood concept here; preserve BOTH scientific names and the alternative-taxonomy caution rather than silently dismissing the FNA treatment. Do not create a duplicate Populus trichocarpa card.
native_range_note: POWO native range lists Alaska, Western Canada, western states, Baja California Norte; Texas not listed. Central Texas native-range or introduced/invasive badge has NOT been certified. County nativity research remains deferred.
